ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Induction in shock

A 72-year-old in septic shock needs intubation. His pressure is 82/46 mm Hg despite initial treatment. The team discusses induction drugs and plans hemodynamic support. Which statement best reflects the immediate concern?

  1. Induction and positive-pressure ventilation may worsen cardiovascular instability
  2. Any induction agent guarantees stable blood pressure
  3. Paralysis alone provides adequate anesthesia and circulatory support
  4. A normal oxygen saturation excludes peri-intubation arrest risk
  5. The first blood pressure check can wait until the ventilator is connected
Answer and explanation

Induction and positive-pressure ventilation may worsen cardiovascular instability

Critically ill patients may deteriorate with induction and reduced venous return during positive-pressure ventilation.

Option explanations

Induction and positive-pressure ventilation may worsen cardiovascular instability: Critically ill patients may deteriorate with induction and reduced venous return during positive-pressure ventilation.

Any induction agent guarantees stable blood pressure: No agent guarantees hemodynamic stability.

Paralysis alone provides adequate anesthesia and circulatory support: Paralysis is neither anesthesia nor circulatory treatment.

A normal oxygen saturation excludes peri-intubation arrest risk: Oxygen saturation does not measure circulatory reserve.

The first blood pressure check can wait until the ventilator is connected: Close monitoring before, during and after intubation is required.
